title: Exception Handling & File I/O
intro: Exception handling interview questions are a must for every fresher Python screen because they test whether you write defensive code or just happy-path code. This page covers the full try/except/else/finally block (what each clause does — the else runs only when no exception is raised, the finally always runs), Python's exception hierarchy (BaseException → Exception → specific exceptions), raising exceptions with raise, creating custom exception classes by inheriting from Exception, and the file I/O operations that almost always come paired with exception handling (open in read/write/append mode, the with statement as the safe way to close files automatically). Every answer explains what can go wrong, not just what the syntax is — because interviewers ask 'what happens if the file doesn't exist?' right after you give the syntax answer.
